The primary takeaway regarding intra-group conflict is that it serves as a disruptive force within a single unit, where differing opinions or ideas on how to achieve common goals create internal divisions that hinder progress toward collective objectives (note 1.pdf). 

While conflict is an unavoidable product of human interaction and can be necessary for development, intra-group conflict specifically acts as a barrier to efficiency by stalling the group's ability to reach its shared targets (note 1.pdf). Because conflicts are best resolved when addressed at an early stage before they escalate and become intractable, managing these internal disagreements is essential to keeping the group's performance under constant check (note 1.pdf).
